subject: PilotAI MSA - clarification on derivative/productization & telemetry
messages:
From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@pilotai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@pilotai.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on MSA redlines - derivative use & telemetry

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call this morning — PilotAI is excited about moving forward. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and attached an edited order-form / redline focusing on two items that are blocking procurement:

1) Productization / derivative rights: your standard language seems to allow Redwood to retain rights to use customer output for model improvements. PilotAI needs a stronger carveout—we ship models and IP to customers and cannot allow our customer data/outputs to be used to train or enhance general models for any productization. We included a proposed opt-out paragraph in the attached doc.

2) Telemetry and evidence: procurement asked for a short evidence pack listing SOC2 status, telemetry retention limits, and whether token-level logs are accessible to ops/eng. Also need confirmation on encryption/KMS for customer data.

Can you confirm whether the productization carveout is acceptable or share Redwood's preferred compromise? Also attaching our redline for reference.

Attachments: PilotAI_MSA_redline.docx

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Mills
Head of Procurement, PilotAI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@pilotai.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA redlines - derivative use & telemetry

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear summary and the redline. High level: we can get to a procurement-acceptable compromise without a full opt-out that would limit service quality for all customers. Proposed pathway: 

- Productization / training: we offer a customer-specific opt-out for training (explicit order-form checkbox) that prevents Redwood from using customer-provided inputs and outputs to retrain our public models. For customers that need stricter separation, we can offer a dedicated private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with explicit no-training language.

- Derivative rights & productization: we can accept language that prohibits redistributing customer outputs as part of Redwood-authored products or model releases, while retaining rights to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry to operate and secure the service.

- Telemetry and evidence: we will provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), a telemetry retention matrix (90/365/730 day options configurable by agreement), and confirmation that token logs are available only to ops for a short retention window and are KMS-encrypted at rest. We do not surface raw customer logs to third parties without a legal process.

I looped in Laura (legal) and Ben (sales/procurement lead) to confirm recommended redline language and evidence pack. If PilotAI is OK with the order-form opt-out and the private deployment alternative, we can propose an updated MSA and order form by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@pilotai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, legal@pilotai.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA redlines - derivative use & telemetry

Sarah / Hannah — thanks for the context. We reviewed PilotAI's proposed opt-out paragraph. Below are redline suggestions from Redwood legal that attempt to balance PilotAI's productization concerns with our need to maintain and secure the service: 

1) Training & model improvements (proposed):
We propose inserting an Order Form flag named "Training Opt-Out" that, when selected by the Customer, prohibits Redwood from using Customer Content (defined as Customer inputs, outputs, and metadata) to train or improve Redwood's public models or product offerings. Redwood may however use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for system performance and reliability improvements that cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstitute Customer Content.

2) Derivative / productization carveout (proposed):
Redwood will not include Customer Outputs as part of any Redwood-authored dataset or model release. Customer Outputs remain the property of Customer to the extent set forth in the Order Form. Redwood retains the right to provide core service features (search, moderation, embeddings indexing) that transform outputs for delivery of the service, but not to commercialize Customer Outputs outside the contracted service.

3) Evidence & security commitments:
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood will provide a redacted report under NDA.
- Telemetry retention: default 90 days; we can extend to 365 or 730 by Order Form.
- Token logs: accessible to ops/engineering for incident triage only; retention default 30 days for raw logs, 365 for aggregated telemetry.
- KMS: customer-managed keys available for Private deployments; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed storage on request and appropriate SLA.

If PilotAI agrees, Ben can implement the Training Opt-Out checkbox in the commercial proposal and we will prepare an MSA clean copy with the above language. If PilotAI requires a stricter opt-out (no aggregated telemetry at all) we will treat that as an enterprise-level security exception and propose a Private deployment quote.

Please see attached proposed-msao-language.txt with exact wording and an evidence checklist (evidence-soc2-2026.pdf). Happy to hop on a short call to finalize.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@pilotai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, legal@pilotai.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA redlines - derivative use & telemetry

Hannah / Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and the drafted language. PilotAI is generally comfortable with the Order Form Training Opt-Out approach and the non-commercialization carveout for Customer Outputs. A couple of clarifying asks before procurement executes: 

- Please confirm the exact default retention windows that will appear on the Order Form (we want to ensure procurement has the right checkbox options).
- Can you confirm whether the redacted SOC 2 will be sent via secure SFTP (preferred) or shared under NDA via DocuSign gateway?
- We need a clear statement that the Training Opt-Out also covers feature-flagged telemetry (e.g., prompt-level signals used for routing/latency tuning) — PilotAI requires that these signals are excluded from any improvement pipelines when the opt-out is selected.

If you can include those points in the final Order Form language, Procurement will sign and route the MSA. I will ask Legal to pause further redlines until we see the updated doc.

Thanks — I can be on a 15-min call tomorrow morning if helpful.

Sarah
Head of Procurement, PilotAI
Attachment: none
